purpose: Offline gate for release-status consistency across the 2026-10-07 release-status documents and the machine-readable state files that evidence them. It reconciles four surfaces that have drifted apart more than once in this countdown: (a) every C-item status table inside the go/no-go checklist, (b) the checklist verdict (header vs final-verdict section), (c) the countdown plan day rows, and (d) the checked-in JSON state files. It is offline: no network, no socket, no credentials, no environment variables, no database. It never proves live behaviour and never replaces the underlying evidence; it only proves that the documents do not contradict each other or the machine state.
status_cell_rule: The status cell of a row is the first cell after the item id whose text begins with a status glyph, ignoring leading markdown emphasis. A cell that merely ends with a glyph (for example an owner cell reading 'Codex ✅') is never read as the status. A row whose status cannot be resolved this way is a finding, not a default.

NOT_EXECUTED is deliberately not listed as a stale value: the same token legitimately describes the staging evidence bundle elsewhere in the table.

plan_scope.note: A day row that references a C-item must agree with that item's current class: a row that still lists the item as work to do cannot coexist with a checklist row that calls the item closed, and a row marked closed cannot coexist with a checklist row that calls it open. Either way one of the two documents is wrong about scope.

declared_open_items.summary: The countdown plan still lists C04's provider physical backup/PITR and isolated Storage restore as the D-8 unit, while the checklist reports C04 closed and files the remaining provider drill as post-launch hardening that does not block 2026-10-07. Both readings are defensible; which one governs the D-1 freeze and the D-2 Go/No-Go is the owner's scope call and no document is rewritten autonomously.
